family: The certificate-prefix symmetric family, defined for every integer N>=0 by one fixed evaluator in proof.md Section 1 and family.py: N=0 gives 0; B is the smallest integer with B^5>64N^3 and k the smallest prime >=B; if k>=N, or with m=N-k, r=ceil(m/k), t=ceil(sqrt(r)) the guards t>=r or kt<r(r+1) fail, the output is 0; otherwise the first k input bits encode a monic polynomial Q over F_2, tested exactly for irreducibility of prime degree k (Z^(2^k)=Z mod Q and gcd(Q,Z^2+Z)=1; failure outputs 0), and with K=F_2[Z]/(Q) and the remaining m payload bits zero-padded to r blocks a_1..a_r of K, the output is the constant coordinate of sigma_t(y_1..y_r), y_i=a_i^(2^(w_i)-1), w_i=r+2-i. The language L={x: A(x)=1} is in P (hence NP, empty witnesses, W(N)=0) for this one fixed evaluator A.
theorem: For this one total uniform polynomial-time family, hence in NP with empty witnesses, C_B2(F_N) >= 3N - R(N) with R(N)=3k+6(floor(kr/t)+kt+r(r+1)+1)=O(N^(4/5)) for every integer N passing the guards (and the bound extends to all sufficiently large integer N), in the full Li-Yang B2 model at actual input length N=|x|; hence liminf C_B2(F_N)/N >= 3.
